exam.experience: Recommended, not required: security administrator with two years of hands-on experience
exam.launch: CompTIA says on or around November 17, 2026

objectives.title: Threat actors and what drives them
Managing hardware, software and data assets

weeks.title: Computer and IT fundamentals
weeks.outcome: Explain how a computer system works and name the basic parts of an IT environment.

weeks.title: Networking fundamentals
weeks.outcome: Explain how devices communicate within a network and across the internet.

weeks.title: Network communication and protocols
weeks.outcome: Explain how information travels between devices and what happens when someone opens a website or remote service.

weeks.title: Operating systems and security fundamentals
weeks.outcome: Describe the technical environment that security professionals protect.

weeks.title: Domain 1: General Security Concepts
weeks.outcome: Explain core security concepts, change management and cryptographic solutions.

weeks.title: Domain 2, part 1: threats, actors and vectors
weeks.outcome: Describe threats, vulnerabilities, threat actors and how attacks reach an organization.

weeks.title: Domain 2, part 2: vulnerabilities, indicators and AI
weeks.outcome: Identify attack surfaces, read signs of malicious activity and explain AI-related threats.

weeks.title: Domain 3, part 1: architecture models and infrastructure
weeks.outcome: Compare architecture models and choose controls that protect infrastructure.

weeks.title: Domain 3, part 2: data protection and resilience
weeks.outcome: Protect data through its life cycle and plan for recovery.

weeks.title: Domain 4, part 1: controls and assets
weeks.outcome: Apply network, endpoint, application and email controls, and manage assets securely.

weeks.title: Domain 4, part 2: vulnerabilities, monitoring and identity
weeks.outcome: Run vulnerability management, understand monitoring tools and apply identity and access concepts.

weeks.title: Domain 4, part 3: automation, response and investigation
weeks.outcome: Automate safely, run incident response and use evidence in an investigation.

weeks.title: Domain 5: Security Program Management and Oversight
weeks.outcome: Explain governance, risk, third-party management, compliance, audits and awareness.

weeks.title: Complete objective review
weeks.outcome: Find and close gaps across all 27 objectives.

sessions.title: Domain 1 objective review
sessions.detail: Retake mixed questions for objectives 1.1–1.3. A score of 80% or more counts as a review pass for each objective with enough questions.

sessions.title: Domain 2 objective review
sessions.detail: Objectives 2.1–2.6, with attention to indicators of malicious activity.

sessions.title: Domain 5 review and gap plan
sessions.detail: Objectives 5.1–5.6, then open the progress dashboard and list every objective below Reviewed.

sessions.title: Case study: Enterprise identity for a multi-tenant SaaS product

weeks.title: Mock examination and remediation
weeks.outcome: Sit a timed 90-question exam and repair what it reveals.

sessions.title: Timed mock exam A
sessions.detail: Sit it in one 90-minute block, with no notes.

sessions.title: Read every explanation
sessions.detail: Work through all explanations for wrong answers, including why your choice was tempting.

sessions.title: Remediate your weakest domain
sessions.detail: Revisit the recommended lessons, then answer your weak-area questions.

sessions.title: Remediate your next weakest domain
sessions.detail: Repeat with the next weakest objectives.

sessions.title: Performance-based practice
sessions.detail: Complete the configuration, log and sequencing exercises.

sessions.title: Case study: An AI assistant with connected tools

weeks.title: Final examination readiness
weeks.outcome: Show readiness through performance, not by reaching the last week.

sessions.title: Timed mock exam B
sessions.detail: A different 90 questions in one 90-minute block.

sessions.title: Ports, acronyms and cryptography
sessions.detail: Use the ports, acronym and cryptography revision sheets.

sessions.title: IAM and attack recognition
sessions.detail: Use the IAM and attack recognition sheets, then your weak-area questions.

sessions.title: Security operations and incident response
sessions.detail: Use the operations and incident response sheets, and retry any PBQ under 80%.

sessions.title: Final readiness check
sessions.detail: Compare your demonstrated performance with the readiness checklist. Extend your study if any line is not met.

sessions.title: Case study: Healthcare account takeover, from alert to post-incident review

modules.title: IT and Networking Foundations
modules.security: Computers, operating systems, networks and protocols. Prerequisites, not exam domains.
modules.design: Understand how digital products communicate and depend on infrastructure.

modules.title: General Security Concepts
modules.security: CIA, AAA, Zero Trust, controls, change management and cryptography.
modules.design: Secure UX principles, trust, privacy and security trade-offs.

modules.title: Threats and Vulnerabilities
modules.security: Attackers, attacks, malware, vulnerabilities and AI threats.
modules.design: Threat-aware product flows, AI safeguards and secure interactions.

modules.title: Security Architecture
modules.security: Cloud, network architecture, data protection and resilience.
modules.design: Multi-tenant SaaS, secure product architecture and data flows.

modules.title: Security Operations
modules.security: Controls, IAM, monitoring, automation, incident response and investigation.
modules.design: Admin interfaces, permission models, security dashboards and recovery.

modules.title: Security Governance and Risk
modules.security: Governance, risk, third parties, compliance, audits and awareness.
modules.design: Privacy experiences, security requirements and vendor workflows.

modules.title: Exam Readiness

modules.design: Integrated technical and design case studies.

designs.title: Map one screen to the system behind it
designs.deliver: An annotated screen with a labelled system map, one marked trust boundary and one partial-failure state.

designs.title: Design the signed-out and no-access states
designs.deliver: A state matrix plus two sketched screens.

designs.title: Design step-up verification for a high-risk change
designs.deliver: A user flow with key screens, a failure-state list and a short written rationale that names the CIA and AAA goals.

designs.title: Redesign a file-share notification to resist phishing
designs.deliver: Redesigned email, landing page and report flow, with attacker-controlled fields annotated.

designs.title: Threat model a feature before it ships
designs.deliver: A data flow diagram, a ranked abuse-case list, and revised screens for the top three risks.

designs.title: Design a support flow that resists impersonation
designs.deliver: A redesigned support console flow, an agent refusal script and notification copy.

designs.title: Design sign-in under attack
designs.deliver: A login state table, a flow for progressive friction, and alert and recovery screens.

designs.title: Design an AI workflow with permission boundaries
designs.deliver: An action classification table, a confirmation flow and an administrator control and audit screen.

designs.title: Map tenant isolation and data residency
designs.deliver: A data flow diagram with boundaries marked, plus workspace switcher and residency panel designs.

designs.title: Design what happens when the security system fails
designs.deliver: A fail-open, fail-closed or degrade decision table, plus degraded mode and break-glass designs.

designs.title: Design sensitive data display and access
designs.deliver: A field classification table, a protection method per field and designs for the reveal flow.

designs.title: Design data export and deletion
designs.deliver: A flow from request to confirmation, an export delivery design and a set of status messages.

designs.title: Design an email authentication setup wizard
designs.deliver: A setup wizard flow, a hand-off page and a state list covering verification.

designs.title: Design a vulnerability prioritization view
designs.deliver: A list and detail design, an exception flow and a defined priority model.

designs.title: Design a monitoring dashboard and investigation view
designs.deliver: An overview, alert detail and triage design, with an explanation of how noise is reduced.

designs.title: Design enterprise SSO setup
designs.deliver: A setup flow from verification to enforcement, with lockout prevention and diagnostics.

designs.title: Design enterprise role and permission management
designs.deliver: A permission matrix and designs for role editing, effective access and access review.

designs.title: Design a third-party integration and consent experience
designs.deliver: A connection flow, consent screen, reconnection states and an integrations management screen.

designs.title: Design a safe automated response rule
designs.deliver: A rule builder, dry run, safeguards and run history design.

designs.title: Design account compromise investigation and recovery
designs.deliver: An incident journey map and designs for lockdown, change review and recovery.

designs.title: Design an administrator audit log
designs.deliver: An event schema with examples, plus search, detail and export designs.

designs.title: Write security requirements during discovery
designs.deliver: A one-page security requirements document and a risk register with at least five risks.

designs.title: Design a vendor security review workflow
designs.deliver: An intake and tiering flow, a review dashboard and a vendor life cycle diagram.

designs.title: Design privacy controls and consent
designs.deliver: A layered consent flow, a privacy center and a data-use map.

designs.title: Enterprise identity for a multi-tenant SaaS product
designs.deliver: A life cycle map, an access view design and a design decision record.

designs.title: An AI assistant with connected tools
designs.deliver: A data flow diagram, an action permission table and administrator control designs.

designs.title: Healthcare account takeover, from alert to post-incident review
designs.deliver: An incident journey, investigation view and post-incident review with product actions.

tables.caption: Acronyms from the lessons
rows: Attribute-based access control: decisions using attributes.
Access control list: a list of who can do what with a resource.
Advanced Encryption Standard: the main symmetric algorithm in use today.
Annualized loss expectancy: expected yearly cost.
Application programming interface: a defined way for programs to talk to each other.
Advanced persistent threat: a skilled attacker with long-term access.
Annualized rate of occurrence: expected events per year.
Address Resolution Protocol: finds the MAC address for an IP address on the local network.
Brand Indicators for Message Identification: shows a verified logo.
Bring your own device: rules for personal devices.
A test meant to separate people from bots, which attackers can imitate.
Classless Inter-Domain Routing: writing a network with a prefix length, such as /24.
Central processing unit: the part that executes instructions.
Certificate revocation list: a published list of revoked certificates.
Cloud security posture management: finds cloud misconfigurations.
Certificate signing request: a request containing a public key and identity details.
Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures: unique IDs for known flaws.
Common Vulnerability Scoring System: a 0 to 10 severity scale.
Common Weakness Enumeration: a catalogue of weakness types.
Distributed denial of service: overwhelming a target from many sources.
Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol: automatically assigns network settings.
DomainKeys Identified Mail: signs outgoing mail.
Data loss prevention: stops sensitive data from leaving.
A policy for handling mail failing SPF or DKIM checks.
Domain Name System: translates names into IP addresses.
Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge: the four steps of a DHCP exchange.
Elliptic curve cryptography: asymmetric cryptography with shorter keys.
Endpoint detection and response: detects and responds on endpoints.
File Transfer Protocol: unencrypted file transfer.
Group Managed Service Accounts: Windows service accounts with automatic password management.
Human Resources, involved in employee matters.
Hardware security module: a dedicated device for protecting keys.
Hypertext Transfer Protocol: the request and response protocol of the web.
Infrastructure as a Service: rented virtual servers, storage and networking.
Internet Control Message Protocol: used for error and status messages.
Internet of Things: connected everyday devices.
Internet Protocol Address Management: tracks address allocation.
A protocol suite that secures IP traffic, often used for VPNs.
The 32-bit version of IP, written as four decimal numbers.
The 128-bit version of IP, written in hexadecimal.
Code that runs in the browser on a web page.
JSON Web Token: a compact signed set of claims.
Local area network: a network in one limited area.
Lightweight Directory Access Protocol: queries directories.
Large language models: AI systems that generate text.
Mobile device management: central control of mobile devices.
Multifactor authentication: using two or more different factor types.
Memorandum of agreement: more specific responsibilities.
Memorandum of understanding: a general statement of intent.
Master services agreement: general terms for future work.
Mean time between failures: average operating time between failures.
Mean time to repair: the average time to fix a failure.
